transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{1} [MAT 2009 1B] Find the shortest distance from the origin to \(x^2+y^2+6x+8y=75\).}
\text{\[(x+3)^2+(y+4)^2=100\]\[C=(-3,-4)\]\[r=10,\quad OC=5\]The origin is inside the circle. The nearest point is on the ray from C through O.\[d=10-5=5\]}
\text{\textbf{2} [MAT 2016 1I] For positive a,b and \(x^2+y^2\le1\), find the greatest possible value of ax+by.}
\text{The parallel lines \(ax+by=k\) sweep across the unit disk. The maximum occurs when the line is tangent, at distance 1 from the origin.\[\frac{k}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}=1\]\[k=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\]}
\text{\textbf{3} [MAT 2007 1D] Which point on \((x-5)^2+(y-4)^2=4\) is closest to \((x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=1\)?}

transcription.tex: \text{A triangle is inscribed in a circle when all three vertices lie on the circle.}
\text{The circle circumscribes the triangle. It is called the circumcircle; its centre is the circumcentre.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{If \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), AC is the diameter of the circumcircle.}
\text{Conversely, if AC is a diameter and B is on the circle, \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\). Thus AB is perpendicular to BC and \(AB^2+BC^2=AC^2\).}
\text{To find the circumcentre of any triangle: find the perpendicular bisectors of two sides, then solve for their intersection.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{a: method 1} Show AB is a diameter using Pythagoras.}
\text{\[AC^2=4^2+8^2=80\]\[BC^2=8^2+4^2=80\]\[AB^2=12^2+4^2=160\]Since \(AC^2+BC^2=AB^2\), angle ACB is a right angle. AB is a diameter.}
\text{\textbf{a: method 2} Show the two sides are perpendicular.}
\text{\[m_{AC}=2,\quad m_{BC}=-\frac12\]The gradients multiply to −1, so \(\angle ACB=90^\circ\).}

transcription.tex: \text{[STEP] A circle touches all three sides of the triangle bounded by \(y=0\), \(3y=4x\) and \(4y+3x=15\). Find its equation.}
\text{Given: the family \((x-2t)^2+(y-t)^2=t^2\), t>0, touches the first two lines. The incircle lies entirely inside the triangle.}
\text{Tangency to y=0 gives centre (h,t) and radius t>0. For a centre inside the triangle, its distance to \(4x-3y=0\) gives\[\frac{4h-3t}{5}=t\Rightarrow h=2t\]}
\text{The distance from (2t,t) to \(3x+4y=15\) is t. Inside the triangle,\[\frac{15-10t}{5}=t\Rightarrow t=1\]}
